diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $\mu_0$ admits a finite $4p$-th moment, then the $2p$-th moments of $\mu_t$ are bounded uniformly in $t$.

issues.failure_explanation: No assumption on the initial law mu_0 is stated in the theorem (nor in thm:continuous diffusion final convergence and lem:KL between dynamic and moving target on which it rests). The proof makes the bound small by multiplying delta by KL(mu_0|pi_{tau(0)}), which requires KL(mu_0|pi_{tau(0)})<infinity, and the c|dot-tau| tracking bound in lem:KL between dynamic and moving target uses uniform second moments of mu_t, which lemma:mu_t bounded moments only supplies when mu_0 has a finite fourth moment. For an initial law with KL(mu_0|pi_{tau(0)})=infinity (e.g., a Dirac measure, which the statement as written admits) the final delta-estimate is vacuous, so convergence is not established.

failure_location.quote:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add to cor:final convergence continuous (and the two supporting lemmas) the standing hypothesis that mu_0 has a finite fourth moment and KL(mu_0|pi_{tau(0)})<infinity (e.g., mu_0=pi_{tau(0)}); all conclusions and the qualitative character of the results are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The continuous-time forward-KL bound and the main continuous-time convergence theorem are unproved for general initial laws; they hold only after restricting mu_0.
issues.title: Missing hypotheses on the initial law in the continuous-time convergence results
issues.why_classification: A standard initialization condition, paralleling the discrete-time theorem's finite-third-moment assumption, closes the gap with no change to any conclusion, rate, or regime.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the Moreau envelope is differentiable and its gradient is globally Lipschitz with constant bounded by $\lip/(1-\tau\lip)$
They analyze this path under the assumptions that the potential $U$ is differentiable, has a Lipschitz-continuous and dissipative gradient, and is \(\alpha \)-weakly convex and convex outside a ball.

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion range invokes the gradient Lipschitz constant L and the proof bounds the Lipschitz constant of the Moreau envelope's gradient by L/(1-tau*L), but Lipschitz continuity of nabla U is not among the stated hypotheses (it appears only in the surrounding prose). The hypothesis is necessary, not merely convenient: at tau=0 the path equals the target, so Ass_drift's uniform smoothness requirement forces nabla U itself to be Lipschitz; without it no uniform-in-tau Lipschitz bound on the path's gradients can hold as tau approaches 0.

failure_location.quote: If  $U$ is $\alpha$-weakly convex and differentiable, $\nabla U$ is dissipative, and $U$ is convex outside a ball, then the path \( (p_\tau)_{\tau \in [0, \bar{\tau}]} \) \cref{eq:daz path} satisfies \Cref{Ass_drift} on $[0,\overline{\tau}]$ for any $\overline{\tau}\in(0,1/\alpha\wedge 1/\lip)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add 'nabla U is Lipschitz-continuous' to the hypotheses, matching the assumption list stated in the adjacent prose and in the cited analysis.
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the proposition does not establish that the Moreau-envelope (DAZ) path satisfies Ass_drift; the abstract convergence results apply to this path only once the missing regularity is imposed.
issues.title: Lipschitz continuity of the gradient omitted from the DAZ path proposition's hypotheses
issues.why_classification: A one-line hypothesis addition, already present verbatim in the surrounding text, restores the statement with no change to any conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: As shown in~\citep[Lemma 3.2]{cordero2025non}, the Eigenvalues of $\nabla^2 \log p_\tau(x)$ are bounded uniformly in $\tau$ and $x$ and, thus, the result follows.

issues.failure_explanation: The identity the proof derives for d_tau log p_tau carries an overall singular factor 1/(1-tau). Uniform bounds on the eigenvalues of the Hessian of log p_tau only give |grad log p_tau(x)| <= C(1+|x|) and |Delta log p_tau| <= C, which yield |d_tau U_tau(x)| <= C(|x|^2+1)/(1-tau), so the concluding inference ('thus, the result follows') is invalid: the singularity cannot be removed by the cited input. The statement is in fact false on the closed interval: the admissible target p_0 = N(m, I) with m != 0 satisfies every hypothesis of prop:convolution_ass (U(x)=|x-m|^2/2 is smooth, strongly convex, with Lipschitz gradient), and for it p_tau = N(sqrt(1-tau) m, I), so d_tau U_tau(x) = - m^T(x - sqrt(1-tau) m)/(2 sqrt(1-tau)), which is unbounded as tau approaches 1 whenever m^T x != 0. Hence no constant c exists for tau in [0,1]; the bound holds only on [0, tau-bar] with tau-bar < 1.

failure_location.quote: There exists $c>0$ such that the density \cref{eq convolution path} satisfies for $\tau\in[0,1]$, $|\partial_\tau  U_\tau(x)| \leq c(|x|^2+1)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the path (lemma and proposition) to [0, tau-bar] with tau-bar < 1 and require the schedule to satisfy tau(0) <= tau-bar; on such intervals the cited Hessian bounds do imply |d_tau U_tau(x)| <= c(tau-bar)(|x|^2+1), with c(tau-bar) deteriorating as tau-bar approaches 1. An alternative is to weaken the growth condition in Ass_drift to an integrable singularity in tau and re-derive the tracking estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The convolutional (variance-preserving) path underlying annealed Langevin sampling and diffusion models is not covered by the framework on the full interval [0,1]: Ass_drift fails arbitrarily close to the Gaussian end, so the abstract convergence theorems do not apply to this path with a schedule starting at tau(0)=1 (as in the paper's own experiments, tau(t)=e^{-t/T}).
issues.title: Quadratic growth bound for the convolutional path fails at the pure-noise end (tau approaching 1)
issues.why_classification: A labelled lemma and the proposition built on it are false as stated; the supported repair narrows the advertised parameter range and constrains the schedule, a limited weakening that leaves a comparable coverage result but genuinely loses the claimed uniform bound up to tau=1.

issues.failure_explanation: With U_tau = -log p_tau as defined in the proposition, U_tau(x) = |Ax-y|^2/(2 sigma^2) + U_X^tau(x) + log Z_tau + const, where Z_tau = integral of p_{Y|X}(y|x) p_X^tau(x) dx is the evidence under the tau-dependent prior (the text's division by the tau-independent p_Y(y) is not the correct normalizer for tau != 0). Hence d_tau U_tau = d_tau U_X^tau + d_tau log Z_tau with d_tau log Z_tau = -E_{p_tau}[d_tau U_X^tau] generally nonzero, so the asserted equality is false and the displayed prose formula is misnormalized. The growth bound itself still transfers, because the missing term is x-independent and bounded by c(E_{p_tau}|X|^2 + 1) <= c via the uniform moments implied by dissipativity.

failure_location.quote: Finally, $\partial_\tau U_\tau=\partial_\tau U_X^\tau$ because the likelihood term does not depend on $\tau$, so the growth condition transfers directly.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the equality by d_tau U_tau = d_tau U_X^tau + d_tau log Z_tau and note |d_tau log Z_tau| <= sup_tau E_{p_tau}[c(|X|^2+1)] < infinity; correct the displayed normalization to the tau-dependent evidence.
issues.overall_effect: The transfer of the quadratic-growth condition to posterior paths is justified by a false argument and the accompanying prose formula is misnormalized; the proposition's conclusion remains correct.
issues.title: False identification d_tau U_tau = d_tau U_X^tau in the posterior-path proof ignores the tau-dependent evidence
issues.why_classification: The false step is repaired by adding a single bounded, x-independent term using moment bounds already established in the paper; no hypothesis, conclusion, or guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $(h_k)_k$ be bounded and satisfy $\step_k<\dissi_{\tau(t_k)}/\lip_{\tau(t_k)}^2$. Then it holds

issues.failure_explanation: The fixed point s-hat_k = h_k/(1-exp(-2 a h_k + 2 L^2 h_k^2)) blows up as h_k approaches the upper boundary a/L^2 from below (the exponent tends to 0), so boundedness of (h_k) does not imply sup_k s-hat_k < infinity, contradicting the claimed step. The conclusion is genuinely false in this regime: take a constant path with a_tau = L_tau = 1 (e.g., pi_tau = N(0,I) for all tau, which satisfies Ass_drift with a=L=1) and h_k = 1 - 1/(k+2) < 1 = a/L^2, which is bounded. Then 1 - 2 h_j + 2 h_j^2 = 1 - 2/(j+2) + O(j^{-2}), so the product from j=i+1 to k-1 is comparable to (i/k)^2 and the sum in (eq step size condition) grows like k/3, tending to infinity. Hence the step-size condition is not implied by the stated hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: Since the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:fixed point phi} is bounded for $h_k$ bounded (note that it converges to $1/(2\dissi)$ as $h_k\rightarrow 0$), it follows that $\sup_k \hat s_k\leq M<\infty$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis with a uniform margin, e.g., h_k <= (1-theta) a_{tau(t_k)}/L_{tau(t_k)}^2 for some theta > 0 (or h_k tending to 0); then 2 a h_k - 2 L^2 h_k^2 >= 2 theta a h_k, the fixed points are uniformly bounded, and the proof goes through; alternatively sharpen the second-moment recursion in lem_second moments of discretization remain bounded.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform-in-k constant in the one-step descent lemma and in the final discrete KL bound rests on sup_k E|X_{t_k}|^2 < infinity, for which lem_second moments of discretization remain bounded requires condition (eq step size condition); lem:added-1 is the only justification given for that condition, so both discrete-time bounds are unproved in the boundary regime h_k approaching a/L^2. The headline discrete convergence theorem corr discrete convergence is unaffected because sum h_k^2 < infinity forces h_k to 0, which itself supplies the missing margin.
issues.title: lem:added-1 is false: bounded step sizes below the stability threshold do not imply the step-size condition
issues.why_classification: An auxiliary lemma is false, but the only regime lost (step sizes tending to the stability boundary) is a degenerate case excluded by a one-line margin condition that the main discrete theorem already satisfies via vanishing step sizes; every advertised conclusion and rate survives.

issues.failure_explanation: Approximation h_n to h in W^{2,1}(R^d) yields convergence of gradients only in L^1, and boundedness of q does not upgrade this to the L^2(nu)-convergence of gradients required for the Dirichlet (right-hand) side of the LSI; the asserted convergence is unjustified in the chosen space (the natural space is W^{1,2}, where mollification does converge with gradients in L^2). Because the extension is supplied only for W^{2,1}_loc test functions, lemma:lsi_KL imposes h in W^{2,1}(R^d), a regularity that is never established for the Fokker-Planck density q_t: the paper proves only q_t in W^{1,p}_loc for a.e. t. The comparison KL(mu_t|pi_{tau(t)}) <= (C_LSI/4) integral |grad log(q_t/p_{tau(t)})|^2 d mu_t, which drives the entire continuous-time analysis, is therefore applied outside the verified hypotheses of the only lemma that justifies it.

failure_location.quote: Convergence of the right-hand side of \gls{lsi} follows directly by the approximation in $W^{2,1}(\R^d)$ together with boundedness of $q$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate lemma:lsi_weak for f in W^{1,2}_loc with grad f in L^2(nu) (approximating in W^{1,2} so the Dirichlet form converges; the truncation argument is unchanged), relax lemma:lsi_KL's hypotheses correspondingly, and verify sqrt(q_t/p_{tau(t)}) in W^{1,2}_loc with finite Dirichlet energy for a.e. t using the already-established grad q_t in L^2(R^d x (t_1,t_2)) and the two-sided Gaussian bounds on q_t; equivalently, apply lemma:lsi_KL to the mollified densities q_t^epsilon constructed in the proof of lemma_time_deriv_KL and pass epsilon to 0.
issues.overall_effect: The continuous-time entropy-dissipation inequality, and with it the forward-KL bound and the continuous-time convergence theorem, rest on an LSI-KL comparison whose applicability to weak Fokker-Planck solutions is not established as written. The discrete-time analysis is unaffected, since its Gaussian-smoothed density does lie in W^{2,1}(R^d) for positive times.
issues.title: LSI extension for nonsmooth test functions is set up in W^{2,1}; the KL-LSI comparison is then applied to q_t outside its verified hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The statements and all downstream conclusions are correct; the gap is closed by a standard change of function space (or by applying the comparison to the already-constructed mollified densities), a routine repair using estimates already proved in the paper that changes no claim, constant, or regime.
